text:
sam-docs: Heads up — opened a docs PR for Deckard-13B variants and compatibility notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-catalog/pull/987. Needs a quick pass for limits + example snippets.

anna-docs: On it. Quick question: the PR lists max_seq 4096 for quantized variants but bench notes we got back show stable up to 8192 on orion. Which should we call out?

mike-eng: We shipped two quant profiles. Cold-path quant (q4_k_m) has 4096 safe memory profile by default, but the runtime can support 8192 with the "high-memory" profile. We should mention both and link the runtime profile names.

lucy-devex: +1. Also found a broken anchor in the runtime-compatibility.md link from the model card (line ~72). Link-checker flagged it.

ci-bot: link-checker: 1 failure — sources/docs/model-catalog/deckard-13b.md: anchor '#runtime-profiles' not found.

sam-docs: Thanks — I'll add a short paragraph: "Quant variants: default sequence limit 4096; runtime 'high-memory' profile supports up to 8192 (see runtime profiles doc)." Also plan to add an SDK snippet showing how to request profile.

anna-docs: For the SDK snippet, please use the new SDK v2 shape. Example we should include:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='deckard-13b-q4_k_m', input='Summarize...', runtime_profile='high-memory')
print(resp.text)
```
That shows runtime_profile usage.

mike-eng: Quick nit: runtime_profile param name in SDK is now profile (not runtime_profile) in the v2 beta. We should use the correct arg to avoid confusion.

lucy-devex: Confirmed — API docs show `profile` (string). Could add a one-line note: "If profile omitted, server selects the default memory profile for the variant."

sam-docs: Updated snippet and PR description. Also added a short compatibility table: variant -> default_seq -> high_mem_seq -> notes. Kept it compact.

anna-docs: Nice. Can you also add a one-liner about fallbacks? i.e., when the requested profile isn't available the smart routing may fallback to a compatible variant or region with a note about potential latency. Customer-facing folks asked for that clarity.

sam-docs: Good call — added fallback note and an example policy line pointing to the routing doc.

lucy-devex: I pushed a tiny fix to the link anchor (runtime-profiles -> profiles). Also updated the doc link in the table.

ci-bot: pr-check: doc-lint passed, link-checker passed.

mike-eng: Can we add a brief benchmark note? Something like: "On orion-x GPUs, Deckard-13B-q4_k_m achieves ~35 tok/s at seq=2048; with profile=high-memory measured ~18 tok/s at 8192 (batch=1) — numbers vary by HW." Keep it indicative, not prescriptive.

sam-docs: Added a short benchmark footnote with disclaimers and a link to the benchmarking dashboard.

anna-docs: One more tiny ask — update the code sample comment to show where to swap to an fp16 variant for lower latency. Many customers ask about switching for latency/cost.

sam-docs: Done. Snippet now shows both q4 variant and fp16 example.

lucy-devex: I reviewed and left two copy edits. Also created a follow-up ticket for migrating older model cards that reference the old anchor names.

sam-docs: Great. Who can approve the PR? @anna-docs?

anna-docs: Approved.

sam-docs: Merged. Thanks all — I'll monitor any follow-up feedback from the integration tests. :shipit:
